description: Antares Simulator is an open-source power system simulator for quantifying the adequacy and economic performance of interconnected power systems at short or distant time horizons. It represents a system as areas linked by interconnections, with thermal, hydro and renewable generation and demand time series, and computes security of supply indicators and least-cost dispatch over many Monte Carlo years. The project was started in 2007 by RTE, the French electricity transmission system operator, which is the exclusive copyright owner; RTE International maintains the Antares website. Its intended users are transmission operators, producers, regulators, academics, consultants and NGOs, and the tool is location independent, applicable to any interconnected system from one country to a continent. It is a cross-platform C++ application for Windows and Linux, with source on GitHub and user and technical documentation on read-the-docs. The software was proprietary until 2018, released under GPL version 3 in May 2018, and from version 9.0 (decided January 2024) is licensed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0, free of charge. Caveats: the repository's tags mix release candidates and test tags, so the documentation is the reliable guide to the current release. Simulation uses are adequacy and resilience assessment, capacity planning and optimisation. Related records: it compares with model-pypsa and platform-gridpath.
